summary: A live bearer token pasted into an HTTP node header; the webhook's credential-by-reference is the decoy.

must_not_find.why: The Webhook node references a stored credential by id and name and contains no secret material. That is the correct pattern; flagging it means the reviewer saw the word 'credentials' and stopped reading. All three keywords are the Webhook node's own text, which is NOT in the diff, so only a reviewer that went to that node and quoted it can trip them. 'credentials block' was dropped for the opposite reason: it states no claim and it is the correct finding's own remedy — the stub answer recommends 'reference it from the node's credentials block' — so it punished the right answer whenever that phrase reached the title.

The webhook sets authentication: headerAuth. It is not an open endpoint. 'unauthenticated webhook' was narrowed to 'unauthenticated': the entry missed the obvious title 'Webhook is unauthenticated' because it required the two words adjacent. Nothing else in this file can be called unauthenticated — the planted defect is an embedded token — so the bare word costs no precision.
